questions.stem: When did Microsoft set Windows 10 to reach end of support?

choices.text: Windows 10 has no EOL date set

questions.explanation: Windows 10 is set to end support on October 14, 2025, per the transcript.
questions.trap: Claiming there is no EOL date is wrong; every Microsoft client OS has a published end-of-support date.

questions.stem: Which statement about Windows 11 is correct?

choices.text: It is 64-bit only and drops support for 32-bit CPUs
It runs only on ARM-based hardware
It is the first Windows version to require an Apple-signed kernel

questions.explanation: Windows 11 is 64-bit only and dropped all support for 32-bit CPUs.
questions.trap: Older Windows versions still supported 32-bit CPUs; the change is specific to Windows 11.

questions.stem: A small business buys two new PCs with Windows 11 Home and wants to join them to the company's Active Directory domain. What is the result?

choices.text: Both PCs join the domain normally
Only one PC at a time can be on the domain
Windows 11 Home cannot join a domain; the business needs Pro or Enterprise
Domain join is allowed but BitLocker becomes mandatory

questions.explanation: Windows Home editions cannot join an Active Directory domain; they use a workgroup model. To join a domain, the PCs need Pro or Enterprise.
questions.trap: Home edition is fine on a home or small workgroup network, but domain join is a Pro/Enterprise capability.

questions.stem: Which Windows feature provides full-disk encryption and is available only in Pro and Enterprise editions (not Home)?
questions.explanation: BitLocker is the full-disk encryption feature limited to Pro and Enterprise editions ('BitLocker is for business').
questions.trap: EFS encrypts individual files and folders and is available in all editions, including Home.

questions.stem: What is the correct contrast between EFS and BitLocker on Windows?

choices.text: EFS encrypts the entire disk; BitLocker encrypts individual files
EFS encrypts individual files/folders and is in all editions; BitLocker encrypts the full disk and is Pro/Enterprise only
Both encrypt the whole disk, but EFS requires TPM and BitLocker does not
BitLocker is the macOS encryption tool; EFS is Windows-only

questions.explanation: EFS = individual files/folders, every edition. BitLocker = full-disk encryption, Pro and Enterprise only.
questions.trap: Watch for the swapped version (EFS = whole disk, BitLocker = single files); the mnemonic is 'BitLocker is for Business' and covers the full disk.

questions.stem: What is the maximum supported RAM on 64-bit Windows 10/11 Home?
questions.explanation: 64-bit Windows Home is capped at 128 GB of RAM.
questions.trap: The 4 GB number is the 32-bit Windows ceiling, not the 64-bit Home ceiling. 6 TB is the Enterprise / Pro for Workstations ceiling.

questions.stem: Which Windows edition adds AppLocker, BranchCache, and (in Windows 11) advanced MDM/MAM features and is licensed via volume licensing for large organizations?
questions.explanation: Enterprise is the volume-licensed edition that adds AppLocker, BranchCache, granular UX control, and advanced MDM/MAM in Windows 11.
questions.trap: Pro adds the business toolkit (BitLocker, Hyper-V, domain join) but not AppLocker / BranchCache / advanced MDM.

questions.stem: A developer wants to run Hyper-V on a Windows 11 laptop. Which is the lowest edition that supports it?
questions.explanation: Hyper-V is part of the Pro business toolkit (alongside BitLocker, domain join, RDP host, and group policy).
questions.trap: Hyper-V is NOT in Home. You don't need to jump all the way to Enterprise; Pro is enough.

questions.stem: Which statement about Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) and Windows editions is correct?

choices.text: Home can only be an RDP client; Pro and Enterprise can be an RDP host
All editions can act as both RDP client and RDP host
Home can be an RDP host; Pro can only be the client
RDP is not supported on Windows 11 at all

questions.explanation: Windows Home can only act as an RDP client (connect out). Pro and Enterprise can act as an RDP host (accept incoming sessions).
questions.trap: The reversed claim (Home as host, Pro as client only) is the trap; remember Home connects outward, business editions also accept inbound.

questions.stem: Two Windows 11 hardware requirements that are mandatory regardless of edition are:

choices.text: ReFS file system and BitLocker enabled

questions.explanation: Windows 11 mandates TPM 2.0 and a UEFI BIOS on every edition.
questions.trap: ReFS is a Pro for Workstations feature, not a Windows 11 mandate. BitLocker is not required to install.
